content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 (no action): predicted service level is 90.2% for 13:15-19:45, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"Both queues are running above forecast with no clear cause. General is +31% (1,704 vs 1,300) and payments is +17% (2,100 vs 1,793), and payments fell to 6.5% service level at 12:45. Even so, current staffing is predicted to recover over the disruption window to 90.2% overall, with payments at 92.6% and general at 87.9%. Abandons are predicted at 1.9% and rest of day at 89.9%. Every option clears the target, so the cheapest one that follows policy is to do nothing. No escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["P1 (free levers: break delay, moving 2 payments agents to general, evening callback) predicts slightly worse results than doing nothing: 89.0% overall and 2.1% abandons. It also lowers payments to 91.6%, so it adds risk to the other queue for no gain.","P2 (adding chat deflection) costs ₹240 and still predicts slightly below no action, at 89.6%.","P3 (overtime) gives the best result: 92.5% overall, general 90.6% and abandons 1.3%. It costs ₹3,780 for about 2.3 points more.","P4 (balanced) reaches 91.6% with general at 90.1% for ₹2,040, and does not move agents off payments."],"watch":"The surge is unexplained, so check actual volumes against the revised forecast each interval. This matters most on payments, given the 6.5% dip at 12:45. If volumes keep rising or general drops toward 80%, switch to P4 or P3. P3's overtime starts at 13:45, so overtime offers need to go out early."}
